target_domain: Inorganic color pigment discovery and materials chemistry, especially the search for new practical pigments through composition-structure-optical-property and human-color-perception modeling.
core_gap: Current pigment discovery remains largely empirical and serendipitous because there is no robust predictive and inverse design framework that jointly links chemical composition, crystal structure, electronic structure, defect chemistry, particle morphology, synthesis feasibility, stability, toxicity, and perceived color to identify practically useful new pigments.
relations: chemical composition constrains accessible crystal structures and defect states
crystal structure and defects determine electronic structure and optical absorption
optical absorption and particle morphology shape spectral reflectance
spectral reflectance maps to perceived color through human visual response
synthesis conditions determine whether a phase can be obtained and retained
stability, toxicity, and manufacturability filter candidate pigments
inverse design maps desired color and property targets to candidate compositions
autonomous discovery cycles connect prediction, synthesis, characterization, and validation
bottlenecks: predicting perceived color directly from composition and structure is unreliable
the viable pigment subset is narrow within vast inorganic chemical space
metastable phases are difficult to predict, synthesize, and retain
simultaneous optimization of color strength, safety, durability, and cost is hard
spectral novelty may not translate into perceptually meaningful new color
closed-loop pigment discovery remains insufficiently mature
exploration is concentrated in familiar oxide, sulfide, and silicate families
unresolved_tensions: novel spectral response versus limited human color categories
vivid color versus chemical and thermal stability
new composition exploration versus safety and environmental constraints
serendipitous discovery versus systematic predictive design
additional functions such as infrared reflectance versus visual color performance
desired_solution_properties: inverse design from desired perceptual and property targets
multi-objective optimization of color, stability, safety, abundance, and scalability
ability to evaluate metastability and synthesis feasibility
integration of human color perception and spectral novelty metrics
support for high-throughput or autonomous experimental validation
capacity to explore beyond established pigment families while retaining practicality
possible_mechanism_types: surrogate modeling of electronic and optical properties
active learning and closed-loop autonomous experimentation
inspiration_search_hints: computational materials discovery workflows for inorganic compounds
color science models of human perception and gamut
autonomous laboratory loops used for materials synthesis
high-throughput screening of stable and metastable phases
multi-objective optimization in safe and durable materials design
exploration of oxide, sulfide, silicate, and related inorganic families for unusual optical responses
functional color materials with coupled thermal or environmental behavior
